paragraphs: Rabbi Levi, son of Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani.

Yuchasin and [Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1046&lang=en) cite this from [Berakhot 28b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.28b.21-22). Hyman says that the old printings indeed read this way, but it is a printing error. The reading should follow the correction in the Vilna printing: Rabbi Levi says that the blessing concerning the Sadducees was instituted at Yavneh. Asked what it corresponds to, Rabbi Levi answers: [according to] Rabbi Hillel son of Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani, it corresponds to “The God of glory thunders,” since Rabbi Hillel derives the eighteen blessings from the psalm “Ascribe to the Lord,” etc.; [according to] Rav Yosef, it corresponds to “One” in the Shema; [according to] Rabbi Tanchum reporting Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, it corresponds to the small vertebra in the spine. Hyman regards this as clear.[^1][^2]
Hyman says that the author of Otzar Yisrael likewise erred in this.

notes.text: The linked Berakhot gives Rabbi Levi addressing Rabbi Hillel, son of Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani. [Heilprin’s Hillel entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1046&lang=en) also cites this folio and lists a Rabbi Levi as Hillel’s brother.

Hyman follows the Vilna correction and reads the three explanations as the accounts of Hillel, Rav Yosef and Rabbi Tanchum in Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi’s name. He treats the older reading as a printing error, and states his conclusion emphatically.
